# Page: IgFold Model

# IgFold Model

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [igfold/model/IgFold.py](igfold/model/IgFold.py)
- [igfold/model/components/IPABlock.py](igfold/model/components/IPABlock.py)
- [igfold/model/components/IPATransformer.py](igfold/model/components/IPATransformer.py)
- [igfold/model/interface.py](igfold/model/interface.py)
- [igfold/utils/transforms.py](igfold/utils/transforms.py)

</details>



The IgFold model is the core deep learning architecture for antibody structure prediction. This document covers the neural network components, forward pass flow, and architectural design of the main prediction model. For information about the processing pipeline that feeds into this model, see [Processing Pipeline](#5.2). For details about training and optimization, see [Training and Loss Functions](#7.2).

## Architecture Overview

The IgFold model follows a multi-stage architecture that combines sequence embeddings, template information, and geometric constraints to predict 3D antibody structures. The model is implemented as a PyTorch Lightning module in the `IgFold` class.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Input Processing"
        INPUT[IgFoldInput] --> CLEAN[clean_input]
        CLEAN --> BERT_FEATS["BERT Features"]
        CLEAN --> BERT_ATTN["BERT Attentions"]
        CLEAN --> TEMP_COORDS["Template Coordinates"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Feature Transformation"
        BERT_FEATS --> STR_NODE[str_node_transform]
        BERT_ATTN --> STR_EDGE[str_edge_transform] 
        STR_NODE --> NODES["Node Features"]
        STR_EDGE --> EDGES["Edge Features"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Graph Processing"
        NODES --> MAIN_BLOCK[main_block]
        EDGES --> MAIN_BLOCK
        MAIN_BLOCK --> GT_EMBS["Graph Transformer Embeddings"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Template Processing"
        TEMP_COORDS --> KABSCH[get_coords_tran_rot]
        KABSCH --> TEMP_TRANS["Template Translations"]
        KABSCH --> TEMP_ROT["Template Rotations"]
        GT_EMBS --> TEMPLATE_IPA[template_ipa]
        TEMP_TRANS --> TEMPLATE_IPA
        TEMP_ROT --> TEMPLATE_IPA
        TEMPLATE_IPA --> STRUCT_EMBS["Structure Embeddings"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Structure Prediction"
        STRUCT_EMBS --> STRUCTURE_IPA[structure_ipa]
        GT_EMBS --> STRUCTURE_IPA
        STRUCTURE_IPA --> COORDS["3D Coordinates"]
        STRUCTURE_IPA --> TRANSLATIONS["Translations"]
        STRUCTURE_IPA --> QUATERNIONS["Quaternions"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Confidence Prediction"
        BERT_FEATS --> DEV_NODE[dev_node_transform]
        BERT_ATTN --> DEV_EDGE[dev_edge_transform]
        DEV_NODE --> DEV_IPA[dev_ipa]
        DEV_EDGE --> DEV_IPA
        TRANSLATIONS --> DEV_IPA
        QUATERNIONS --> DEV_IPA
        DEV_IPA --> DEV_LINEAR[dev_linear]
        DEV_LINEAR --> PRMSD["Predicted RMSD"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output"
        COORDS --> OUTPUT[IgFoldOutput]
        PRMSD --> OUTPUT
        TRANSLATIONS --> OUTPUT
        QUATERNIONS --> OUTPUT
    end
```

Sources: [igfold/model/IgFold.py:19-488]()

## Input and Output Interfaces

The model uses structured dataclasses to define its input and output specifications.

### IgFoldInput

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `embeddings` | `List[List[torch.FloatTensor]]` | BERT embeddings for each chain |
| `attentions` | `List[List[torch.FloatTensor]]` | BERT attention matrices |
| `template_coords` | `Optional[torch.FloatTensor]` | Template structure coordinates |
| `template_mask` | `Optional[torch.BoolTensor]` | Mask for valid template positions |
| `batch_mask` | `Optional[torch.BoolTensor]` | Mask for valid sequence positions |
| `align_mask` | `Optional[torch.BoolTensor]` | Mask for alignment during training |
| `coords_label` | `Optional[torch.FloatTensor]` | Ground truth coordinates for training |
| `return_embeddings` | `Optional[bool]` | Whether to return intermediate embeddings |

### IgFoldOutput

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `coords` | `torch.FloatTensor` | Predicted 3D coordinates |
| `prmsd` | `torch.FloatTensor` | Predicted RMSD confidence scores |
| `translations` | `torch.FloatTensor` | Rigid body translations |
| `rotations` | `torch.FloatTensor` | Rigid body rotations |
| `coords_loss` | `Optional[torch.FloatTensor]` | Coordinate prediction loss |
| `bondlen_loss` | `Optional[torch.FloatTensor]` | Bond length constraint loss |
| `prmsd_loss` | `Optional[torch.FloatTensor]` | Confidence prediction loss |
| `loss` | `Optional[torch.FloatTensor]` | Total training loss |

Sources: [igfold/model/interface.py:1-40]()

## Core Components

### Graph Transformer Block

The `main_block` is a `TriangleGraphTransformer` that processes sequence-level features extracted from BERT embeddings and attentions.

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Graph Transformer Processing"
        BERT_FEATS["BERT Features<br/>(B, L, 512)"] --> STR_NODE_TRANS[str_node_transform]
        BERT_ATTN["BERT Attentions<br/>(B, L, L, 64)"] --> STR_EDGE_TRANS[str_edge_transform]
        
        STR_NODE_TRANS --> NODE_DIM["Node Features<br/>(B, L, node_dim)"]
        STR_EDGE_TRANS --> EDGE_DIM["Edge Features<br/>(B, L, L, node_dim)"]
        
        NODE_DIM --> TRIANGLE_GT[TriangleGraphTransformer]
        EDGE_DIM --> TRIANGLE_GT
        
        TRIANGLE_GT --> GT_NODES["Updated Nodes"]
        TRIANGLE_GT --> GT_EDGES["Updated Edges"]
    end
```

The transformations use linear layers followed by ReLU activation and LayerNorm:

```mermaid
graph LR
    INPUT["Input Features"] --> LINEAR[Linear Layer]
    LINEAR --> RELU[ReLU Activation]
    RELU --> LAYERNORM[LayerNorm]
    LAYERNORM --> OUTPUT["Transformed Features"]
```

Sources: [igfold/model/IgFold.py:50-75](), [igfold/model/IgFold.py:239-245]()

### Invariant Point Attention (IPA) Components

The model employs three different IPA modules for different purposes:

1. **Template IPA** (`template_ipa`): Processes template structural information
2. **Structure IPA** (`structure_ipa`): Predicts 3D coordinates with rigid body transformations  
3. **Deviation IPA** (`dev_ipa`): Estimates confidence scores

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "IPA Architecture Components"
        NODES["Node Features"] --> IPA_ENCODER[IPAEncoder]
        TRANSLATIONS["Translations"] --> IPA_ENCODER
        ROTATIONS["Rotations"] --> IPA_ENCODER
        PAIRWISE["Pairwise Repr"] --> IPA_ENCODER
        
        IPA_ENCODER --> UPDATED_NODES["Updated Node Features"]
        
        NODES2["Node Features"] --> IPA_TRANSFORMER[IPATransformer]
        PAIRWISE2["Pairwise Repr"] --> IPA_TRANSFORMER
        
        IPA_TRANSFORMER --> COORDS["3D Coordinates"]
        IPA_TRANSFORMER --> NEW_TRANS["New Translations"]
        IPA_TRANSFORMER --> QUATERNIONS["Quaternions"]
    end
```

Sources: [igfold/model/IgFold.py:76-88](), [igfold/model/IgFold.py:103-108](), [igfold/model/components/IPATransformer.py:16-174]()

## Forward Pass Flow

The model's forward pass follows a structured pipeline:

### 1. Input Processing and Cleaning

The `clean_input` method processes raw inputs, handling missing values and ensuring proper tensor shapes and masks.

```mermaid
graph TD
    INPUT[IgFoldInput] --> EXTRACT["Extract Components"]
    EXTRACT --> CHECK_NONE["Check for None Values"]
    CHECK_NONE --> CREATE_DEFAULTS["Create Default Tensors"]
    CREATE_DEFAULTS --> APPLY_MASKS["Apply Batch/Align Masks"]  
    APPLY_MASKS --> CENTER_COORDS["Center Template Coords"]
    CENTER_COORDS --> CLEANED[Cleaned Input]
```

Sources: [igfold/model/IgFold.py:144-194]()

### 2. Feature Processing

BERT embeddings and attentions are concatenated and transformed into the model's internal feature space.

| Configuration Parameter | Default Value | Description |
|------------------------|---------------|-------------|
| `bert_feat_dim` | 512 | BERT feature dimension |
| `bert_attn_dim` | 64 | BERT attention dimension |
| `node_dim` | configurable | Internal node feature dimension |

Sources: [igfold/model/IgFold.py:32-36](), [igfold/model/IgFold.py:223-245]()

### 3. Template Coordinate Processing

Template coordinates are processed using Kabsch alignment to extract rigid body transformations:

```mermaid
graph LR
    TEMP_COORDS["Template Coords<br/>(B, L*4, 3)"] --> RESHAPE["Reshape to<br/>(B, L, 4, 3)"]
    RESHAPE --> IDEAL_COORDS["Get Ideal Coords"]
    IDEAL_COORDS --> KABSCH[Kabsch Alignment]
    KABSCH --> TRANSLATIONS["Translations<br/>(B, L, 3)"]
    KABSCH --> ROTATIONS["Rotations<br/>(B, L, 3, 3)"]
```

Sources: [igfold/model/IgFold.py:114-142](), [igfold/model/IgFold.py:233-237]()

### 4. Structure Prediction

The `structure_ipa` (`IPATransformer`) predicts final coordinates by iteratively refining translations and quaternions:

```mermaid
graph TD
    STRUCT_NODES["Structure Node Features"] --> IPA_LAYERS["IPA Layers"]
    PAIRWISE["Pairwise Features"] --> IPA_LAYERS
    
    IPA_LAYERS --> LAYER_BLOCK[IPABlock]
    LAYER_BLOCK --> LINEAR_UPDATE[Linear Update]
    LINEAR_UPDATE --> QUAT_UPDATE["Quaternion Update"]
    LINEAR_UPDATE --> TRANS_UPDATE["Translation Update"] 
    
    QUAT_UPDATE --> MULTIPLY[Quaternion Multiply]
    TRANS_UPDATE --> ADD[Translation Add]
    
    MULTIPLY --> NEXT_LAYER["Next Layer or Output"]
    ADD --> NEXT_LAYER
    
    NEXT_LAYER --> FINAL_COORDS["Final 3D Coordinates"]
```

Sources: [igfold/model/IgFold.py:256-263](), [igfold/model/components/IPATransformer.py:83-174]()

### 5. Confidence Prediction

A separate deviation pathway predicts per-residue confidence using the `dev_ipa`:

```mermaid
graph LR
    BERT_FEATS --> DEV_NODE[dev_node_transform]
    BERT_ATTN --> DEV_EDGE[dev_edge_transform]
    PRED_TRANS["Predicted Translations<br/>(detached)"] --> DEV_IPA[dev_ipa]
    PRED_ROT["Predicted Rotations<br/>(detached)"] --> DEV_IPA
    DEV_NODE --> DEV_IPA
    DEV_EDGE --> DEV_IPA
    DEV_IPA --> DEV_LINEAR[dev_linear]
    DEV_LINEAR --> RELU[ReLU]
    RELU --> PRMSD["Predicted RMSD"]
```

Sources: [igfold/model/IgFold.py:265-275]()

## Loss Functions

During training, multiple loss components are computed:

| Loss Component | Function | Purpose |
|---------------|----------|---------|
| `coords_loss` | `kabsch_mse` | Coordinate prediction accuracy |
| `bondlen_loss` | `bond_length_l1` | Bond length constraints |
| `prmsd_loss` | `bb_prmsd_l1` | Confidence prediction accuracy |

Sources: [igfold/model/IgFold.py:287-346]()

## Advanced Features

### Coordinate Scoring

The `score_coords` method allows re-evaluation of confidence scores for given coordinates without full forward pass:

Sources: [igfold/model/IgFold.py:372-403]()

### Gradient Refinement

The `gradient_refine` method performs iterative optimization of predicted structures using violation constraints:

```mermaid
graph TD
    INPUT_COORDS["Input Coordinates"] --> ENABLE_GRAD["Enable Gradients"]
    ENABLE_GRAD --> OPTIMIZER["Adam Optimizer<br/>(lr=2e-2)"]
    OPTIMIZER --> ITER_START["Iteration Loop<br/>(80 steps)"]
    
    ITER_START --> TRANSFORM[transform_ideal_coords]
    TRANSFORM --> CALC_VIOL[violation_loss]
    TRANSFORM --> CALC_RMSD[kabsch_mse]
    
    CALC_VIOL --> TOTAL_LOSS["Total Loss"]
    CALC_RMSD --> TOTAL_LOSS
    TOTAL_LOSS --> BACKWARD[loss.backward]
    BACKWARD --> STEP[optimizer.step]
    STEP --> ITER_END{"More Steps?"}
    
    ITER_END -->|Yes| ITER_START
    ITER_END -->|No| FINAL_COORDS["Refined Coordinates"]
```

Sources: [igfold/model/IgFold.py:427-488]()

## Model Configuration

Key hyperparameters control the model architecture:

| Parameter | Description | Typical Range |
|-----------|-------------|---------------|
| `depth` | Main transformer depth | 4-8 |
| `gt_depth` | Graph transformer depth | 2-4 |
| `gt_heads` | Graph transformer heads | 8-16 |
| `temp_ipa_depth` | Template IPA depth | 2-4 |
| `str_ipa_depth` | Structure IPA depth | 4-8 |
| `dev_ipa_depth` | Deviation IPA depth | 2-4 |

Sources: [igfold/model/IgFold.py:37-48]()

# Page: Processing Pipeline

# Processing Pipeline

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [igfold/utils/embed.py](igfold/utils/embed.py)
- [igfold/utils/folding.py](igfold/utils/folding.py)

</details>



This document covers IgFold's structure prediction pipeline, detailing the sequence of operations that transform antibody sequences into predicted 3D structures. The pipeline orchestrates input processing, sequence embeddings, model inference, and output generation through a series of well-defined stages.

For information about the neural network model components used within this pipeline, see [IgFold Model](#5.1). For details about the data processing utilities that support the pipeline, see [Data Processing Utilities](#5.3).

## Pipeline Overview

The IgFold processing pipeline consists of two main entry points: the `fold()` function for complete structure prediction and the `embed()` function for embedding generation only. Both pipelines share common input processing stages but differ in their outputs and post-processing steps.

### Main Pipeline Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    INPUT[Input Sequences] --> GET_SEQ_DICT["get_sequence_dict()"]
    FASTA[FASTA File] --> GET_SEQ_DICT
    
    GET_SEQ_DICT --> SEQ_DICT["Sequence Dictionary"]
    
    TEMPLATE_PDB[Template PDB] --> PROCESS_TEMPLATE["process_template()"]
    SEQ_DICT --> PROCESS_TEMPLATE
    
    PROCESS_TEMPLATE --> TEMP_COORDS["Template Coordinates"]
    PROCESS_TEMPLATE --> TEMP_MASK["Template Mask"]
    
    SEQ_DICT --> ANTIBERTY["AntiBERTy Embedding"]
    ANTIBERTY --> EMBEDDINGS["Embeddings"]
    ANTIBERTY --> ATTENTIONS["Attentions"]
    
    EMBEDDINGS --> IGFOLD_INPUT["IgFoldInput Object"]
    ATTENTIONS --> IGFOLD_INPUT
    TEMP_COORDS --> IGFOLD_INPUT
    TEMP_MASK --> IGFOLD_INPUT
    
    IGFOLD_INPUT --> MODEL_INFERENCE["Model Inference Loop"]
    MODEL_INFERENCE --> ENSEMBLE_SELECTION["Best Model Selection"]
    
    ENSEMBLE_SELECTION --> PROCESS_PRED["process_prediction()"]
    PROCESS_PRED --> PDB_OUTPUT["PDB Output"]
    PROCESS_PRED --> REFINED_STRUCTURE["Refined Structure"]
```

*Sources: [igfold/utils/folding.py:153-231](), [igfold/utils/embed.py:7-53]()*

### Function-Level Architecture

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Entry Points"
        FOLD_FUNC["fold()"]
        EMBED_FUNC["embed()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Input Processing"
        GET_SEQ["get_sequence_dict()"]
        PROC_TEMPLATE["process_template()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Model Interface"
        IGFOLD_INPUT_CLASS["IgFoldInput"]
        MODEL_CALL["model(model_in)"]
        GRADIENT_REFINE["model.gradient_refine()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Post Processing"
        PROC_PREDICTION["process_prediction()"]
        SAVE_PDB["save_PDB()"]
        WRITE_BFACTOR["write_pdb_bfactor()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Optional Refinement"
        OPENMM_REF["OpenMM refine()"]
        PYROSETTA_REF["PyRosetta refine()"]
        RENUMBER_PDB["renumber_pdb()"]
    end
    
    FOLD_FUNC --> GET_SEQ
    EMBED_FUNC --> GET_SEQ
    
    FOLD_FUNC --> PROC_TEMPLATE
    EMBED_FUNC --> PROC_TEMPLATE
    
    GET_SEQ --> IGFOLD_INPUT_CLASS
    PROC_TEMPLATE --> IGFOLD_INPUT_CLASS
    
    IGFOLD_INPUT_CLASS --> MODEL_CALL
    MODEL_CALL --> GRADIENT_REFINE
    
    FOLD_FUNC --> PROC_PREDICTION
    PROC_PREDICTION --> SAVE_PDB
    PROC_PREDICTION --> WRITE_BFACTOR
    
    PROC_PREDICTION --> OPENMM_REF
    PROC_PREDICTION --> PYROSETTA_REF
    PROC_PREDICTION --> RENUMBER_PDB
```

*Sources: [igfold/utils/folding.py:13-232](), [igfold/utils/embed.py:7-53]()*

## Input Processing

The pipeline begins with sequence input processing through the `get_sequence_dict()` function, which handles multiple input formats and validates the provided data.

### Sequence Input Handling

| Input Type | Processing Method | Output |
|------------|-------------------|--------|
| Direct sequences | Use provided dictionary | `seq_dict` |
| FASTA file | Parse via `get_fasta_chain_dict()` | `seq_dict` |
| Both provided | Prioritize FASTA file with warning | `seq_dict` |
| Neither provided | Exit with error | - |

The function implements a priority system where FASTA files take precedence over direct sequence input when both are provided [igfold/utils/folding.py:13-27]().

### Optional Sequence Truncation

When `truncate_sequences=True`, the pipeline utilizes AbNumber integration to trim sequences to their canonical regions:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    RAW_SEQ["Raw Sequences"] --> TRUNCATE["truncate_seq()"]
    TRUNCATE --> CANONICAL_SEQ["Canonical Sequences"]
    CANONICAL_SEQ --> EMBEDDING["AntiBERTy Embedding"]
```

This feature requires AbNumber installation and processes each sequence through the `truncate_seq()` function [igfold/utils/folding.py:173-179]().

*Sources: [igfold/utils/folding.py:13-27](), [igfold/utils/folding.py:173-179]()*

## Embedding Generation

The pipeline generates sequence embeddings and attention maps using the AntiBERTy model through a standardized interface.

### AntiBERTy Processing

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    SEQ_VALUES["seq_dict.values()"] --> ANTIBERTY["antiberty.embed()"]
    ANTIBERTY --> RAW_EMBEDDINGS["Raw Embeddings"]
    ANTIBERTY --> RAW_ATTENTIONS["Raw Attentions"]
    
    RAW_EMBEDDINGS --> TRIM_EMB["[1:-1] Trim CLS/SEP"]
    RAW_ATTENTIONS --> TRIM_ATT["[:,∶,1:-1,1:-1] Trim"]
    
    TRIM_EMB --> UNSQUEEZE_EMB["unsqueeze(0)"]
    TRIM_ATT --> UNSQUEEZE_ATT["unsqueeze(0)"]
    
    UNSQUEEZE_EMB --> FINAL_EMBEDDINGS["Final Embeddings"]
    UNSQUEEZE_ATT --> FINAL_ATTENTIONS["Final Attentions"]
```

The embedding process strips special tokens (`[CLS]` and `[SEP]`) and adds batch dimensions to prepare data for model input [igfold/utils/folding.py:190-195]().

*Sources: [igfold/utils/folding.py:190-195](), [igfold/utils/embed.py:22-27]()*

## Template Processing

Optional template PDB files are processed through the `process_template()` function, which extracts coordinates and applies masking based on user specifications.

### Template Coordinate Extraction

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    TEMPLATE_PDB["Template PDB"] --> GET_COORDS["get_atom_coords()"]
    GET_COORDS --> ATOM_COORDS["N, CA, C, CB Coordinates"]
    
    ATOM_COORDS --> STACK_COORDS["torch.stack() + reshape"]
    STACK_COORDS --> TEMP_COORDS["Template Coordinates"]
    
    TEMP_COORDS --> CREATE_MASK["Create Boolean Mask"]
    CREATE_MASK --> INVALID_CHECK["Check NaN & Zero Values"]
    INVALID_CHECK --> TEMP_MASK["Template Mask"]
    
    CDR_IGNORE["ignore_cdrs parameter"] --> CDR_MASKING["CDR Region Masking"]
    CHAIN_IGNORE["ignore_chain parameter"] --> CHAIN_MASKING["Chain Masking"]
    
    CDR_MASKING --> TEMP_MASK
    CHAIN_MASKING --> TEMP_MASK
```

### Template Masking Options

The pipeline supports selective template masking through two parameters:

- **CDR Masking**: `ignore_cdrs` parameter accepts boolean, string, or list values to mask specific CDR regions [igfold/utils/folding.py:54-66]()
- **Chain Masking**: `ignore_chain` parameter masks entire heavy ("H") or light ("L") chains [igfold/utils/folding.py:67-73]()

*Sources: [igfold/utils/folding.py:30-75]()*

## Model Inference

The core prediction phase involves creating an `IgFoldInput` object and running inference through an ensemble of models.

### Model Input Construction

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    EMBEDDINGS["Processed Embeddings"] --> IGFOLD_INPUT["IgFoldInput()"]
    ATTENTIONS["Processed Attentions"] --> IGFOLD_INPUT
    TEMP_COORDS["Template Coordinates"] --> IGFOLD_INPUT
    TEMP_MASK["Template Mask"] --> IGFOLD_INPUT
    
    IGFOLD_INPUT --> MODEL_INPUT["Model Input Object"]
    MODEL_INPUT --> INFERENCE["Model Inference Loop"]
```

### Ensemble Prediction Loop

The pipeline runs multiple models and selects the best prediction based on quantile scoring:

| Step | Operation | Output |
|------|-----------|--------|
| 1 | Forward pass: `model(model_in)` | Raw predictions |
| 2 | Gradient refinement: `model.gradient_refine()` | Refined coordinates |
| 3 | Score calculation: `prmsd.quantile(0.9)` | Quality score |
| 4 | Best model selection: `min(scores)` | Final prediction |

The scoring mechanism uses the 90th percentile of predicted RMSD values to identify the most confident prediction [igfold/utils/folding.py:211-220]().

*Sources: [igfold/utils/folding.py:203-220](), [igfold/utils/embed.py:35-44]()*

## Post-Processing and Output

The `process_prediction()` function handles model output formatting, structure refinement, and file generation.

### Output Processing Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    MODEL_OUT["Model Output"] --> REARRANGE_PRMSD["Rearrange pRMSD"]
    REARRANGE_PRMSD --> COORDS_EXTRACT["Extract Coordinates"]
    COORDS_EXTRACT --> CALC_RMSD["Calculate Residue RMSD"]
    
    CALC_RMSD --> SAVE_PDB_CALL["save_PDB()"]
    SAVE_PDB_CALL --> PDB_STRING["PDB String"]
    
    PDB_STRING --> REFINE_CHECK{"do_refine?"}
    REFINE_CHECK -->|Yes| REFINE_CHOICE{"use_openmm?"}
    REFINE_CHECK -->|No| RENUM_CHECK{"do_renum?"}
    
    REFINE_CHOICE -->|Yes| OPENMM_REF["OpenMM Refinement"]
    REFINE_CHOICE -->|No| PYROSETTA_REF["PyRosetta Refinement"]
    
    OPENMM_REF --> RENUM_CHECK
    PYROSETTA_REF --> RENUM_CHECK
    
    RENUM_CHECK -->|Yes| RENUMBER["renumber_pdb()"]
    RENUM_CHECK -->|No| BFACTOR_WRITE["write_pdb_bfactor()"]
    
    RENUMBER --> BFACTOR_WRITE
    BFACTOR_WRITE --> FINAL_PDB["Final PDB Output"]
```

### Refinement Options

The pipeline supports two refinement backends:

- **OpenMM**: Physics-based energy minimization [igfold/utils/folding.py:118-123]()
- **PyRosetta**: Rosetta-based structure optimization [igfold/utils/folding.py:125-131]()

Both refinement methods require separate installation and are imported dynamically with error handling for missing dependencies.

### Output File Generation

The pipeline generates several output files:

| File Type | Content | Function |
|-----------|---------|----------|
| PDB | 3D coordinates with atoms N, CA, C, CB, O | `save_PDB()` |
| FASTA | Sequence information (auto-generated if needed) | Direct file writing |
| B-factor PDB | Structure with confidence scores | `write_pdb_bfactor()` |

*Sources: [igfold/utils/folding.py:78-150]()*

## Pipeline Variants

The system provides two main pipeline variants optimized for different use cases:

### Structure Prediction Pipeline (`fold()`)
- Complete structure prediction workflow
- Optional template integration
- Ensemble model scoring
- Structure refinement and renumbering
- Full PDB output generation

### Embedding Pipeline (`embed()`)
- Embeddings and attention extraction only
- Minimal post-processing
- Returns `IgFoldOutput` with embedding data
- Useful for downstream analysis or custom modeling

The embedding pipeline shares input processing with the full pipeline but bypasses refinement and file generation steps [igfold/utils/embed.py:7-53]().

*Sources: [igfold/utils/folding.py:153-231](), [igfold/utils/embed.py:7-53]()*

---

# Page: Data Processing Utilities

# Data Processing Utilities

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [igfold/utils/constants.py](igfold/utils/constants.py)
- [igfold/utils/coordinates.py](igfold/utils/coordinates.py)
- [igfold/utils/geometry.py](igfold/utils/geometry.py)
- [igfold/utils/pdb.py](igfold/utils/pdb.py)

</details>



This document covers IgFold's core data processing utilities that handle PDB files, coordinate extraction, geometric calculations, and antibody-specific processing. These utilities form the foundation layer that supports the structure prediction pipeline and refinement components.

For information about the overall processing pipeline workflow, see [Processing Pipeline](#5.2). For details about neural network model components, see [IgFold Model](#5.1).

## Overview

The data processing utilities are organized into four main modules that work together to handle structural data:

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "PDB Processing"
        PDB_UTILS["igfold.utils.pdb"]
        PDB_FUNCS["renumber_pdb<br/>get_atom_coords<br/>save_PDB<br/>cdr_indices"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Geometric Operations"
        GEOM_UTILS["igfold.utils.geometry"]
        GEOM_FUNCS["normed_vec<br/>dist<br/>angle<br/>dihedral"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Coordinate Manipulation"
        COORD_UTILS["igfold.utils.coordinates"] 
        COORD_FUNCS["place_fourth_atom<br/>get_ideal_coords<br/>place_o_coords"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Physical Constants"
        CONST_UTILS["igfold.utils.constants"]
        CONST_VALS["BL_N_CA<br/>BA_N_CA_C<br/>VDW_N"]
    end
    
    PDB_UTILS --> PDB_FUNCS
    GEOM_UTILS --> GEOM_FUNCS
    COORD_UTILS --> COORD_FUNCS
    CONST_UTILS --> CONST_VALS
    
    PDB_FUNCS --> COORD_FUNCS
    GEOM_FUNCS --> COORD_FUNCS
    CONST_VALS --> COORD_FUNCS
```

**Sources:** [igfold/utils/pdb.py:1-515](), [igfold/utils/geometry.py:1-77](), [igfold/utils/coordinates.py:1-76](), [igfold/utils/constants.py:1-22]()

## PDB File Processing

The `igfold.utils.pdb` module provides comprehensive tools for reading, writing, and manipulating PDB files. The main data flow processes raw PDB files into structured coordinate tensors:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    INPUT_PDB["PDB File Input"] --> PARSE_PDB["PDBParser.get_structure"]
    FASTA_INPUT["FASTA File (optional)"] --> PARSE_PDB
    
    PARSE_PDB --> EXTRACT_COORDS["get_atom_coords"]
    EXTRACT_COORDS --> ATOM_EXTRACTION["Extract N, CA, C, CB, O coordinates"]
    
    ATOM_EXTRACTION --> MISSING_ATOMS["place_missing_cb_o"]
    MISSING_ATOMS --> COORD_TENSORS["PyTorch Coordinate Tensors"]
    
    COORD_TENSORS --> MASKS["get_atom_coords_mask"]
    MASKS --> FINAL_OUTPUT["Structured Coordinate Data"]
    
    subgraph "Chain Processing"
        CHAIN_COUNT["count_pdb_chains"]
        CHAIN_REORDER["reorder_pdb_chains"] 
        CHAIN_SEQ["get_pdb_chain_seq"]
    end
    
    subgraph "CDR Identification"
        CDR_INDICES["cdr_indices"]
        CDR_RANGES["get_cdr_range_dict"]
        H3_INDICES["h3_indices"]
    end
    
    subgraph "AbNumber Integration"
        RENUMBER["renumber_pdb"]
        ABNUMBER_SERVICE["AbNum Web Service"]
        RENUMBER --> ABNUMBER_SERVICE
    end
```

**Sources:** [igfold/utils/pdb.py:194-251](), [igfold/utils/pdb.py:21-59](), [igfold/utils/pdb.py:314-378]()

### Coordinate Extraction

The primary function `get_atom_coords` extracts backbone and side-chain coordinates from PDB files:

| Function | Purpose | Input | Output |
|----------|---------|--------|--------|
| `get_atom_coords` | Extract all atom coordinates | PDB file, optional FASTA | Dict of coordinate tensors |
| `get_atom_coord` | Get single atom coordinate | Residue, atom type | 3D coordinate array |
| `get_cb_or_ca_coord` | Get CB coordinate (CA fallback) | Residue | 3D coordinate array |
| `place_missing_cb_o` | Fill missing CB and O atoms | Coordinate dict | Updated coordinates |

**Sources:** [igfold/utils/pdb.py:194-251](), [igfold/utils/pdb.py:120-137](), [igfold/utils/pdb.py:160-192]()

### Chain Management

Chain processing functions handle multi-chain antibody structures:

- `count_pdb_chains`: Returns the number of chains in a PDB file [igfold/utils/pdb.py:61-68]()
- `reorder_pdb_chains`: Reorders chains according to specified sequence [igfold/utils/pdb.py:71-117]()
- `get_pdb_chain_seq`: Extracts amino acid sequence from specific chain [igfold/utils/pdb.py:294-311]()

### CDR Loop Identification

Antibody-specific processing includes CDR (Complementarity Determining Region) identification using Chothia numbering:

```mermaid
graph TD
    CHOTHIA_PDB["Chothia Numbered PDB"] --> CDR_FUNC["cdr_indices"]
    CDR_TYPE["CDR Type (h1, h2, h3, l1, l2, l3)"] --> CDR_FUNC
    
    CDR_FUNC --> CHOTHIA_RANGES["Chothia Range Dictionary"]
    CHOTHIA_RANGES --> BINARY_SEARCH["Binary Search on Residue IDs"]
    BINARY_SEARCH --> CDR_START_END["CDR Start/End Indices"]
    
    subgraph "CDR Ranges"
        H1["h1: (26, 32)"]
        H2["h2: (52, 56)"]
        H3["h3: (95, 102)"]
        L1["l1: (24, 34)"]
        L2["l2: (50, 56)"]
        L3["l3: (89, 97)"]
    end
```

**Sources:** [igfold/utils/pdb.py:314-378](), [igfold/utils/pdb.py:381-402]()

## Geometric Calculations

The `igfold.utils.geometry` module provides fundamental geometric operations for structural calculations:

| Function | Purpose | Formula |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `normed_vec` | Vector normalization | `vec / ||vec||` |
| `dist` | Euclidean distance | `sqrt(sum((x1-x2)²))` |
| `angle` | Bond angle | `arccos(a·b)` |
| `dihedral` | Dihedral angle | `atan2(y, x)` using cross products |
| `coords_to_frame` | Local coordinate frame | N-CA-C backbone frame |

**Sources:** [igfold/utils/geometry.py:7-77]()

### Reference Frame Calculations

The `coords_to_frame` function converts backbone coordinates into local reference frames for structural analysis:

```mermaid
graph LR
    COORDS["Backbone Coordinates<br/>(N, CA, C, O)"] --> VECTORS["Vector Calculations"]
    VECTORS --> CA_N["CA-N vector"]
    VECTORS --> CA_C["CA-C vector"]
    
    CA_N --> N1["n1 = normalized CA-N"]
    CA_C --> N2["n2 = cross(n1, CA-C)"]
    N1 --> N3["n3 = cross(n1, n2)"]
    N2 --> N3
    
    N1 --> ROTATION_MATRIX["Rotation Matrix [n1, n2, n3]"]
    N2 --> ROTATION_MATRIX
    N3 --> ROTATION_MATRIX
    
    ROTATION_MATRIX --> LOCAL_FRAME["Local Coordinate Frame"]
```

**Sources:** [igfold/utils/geometry.py:61-77]()

## Coordinate Manipulation

The `igfold.utils.coordinates` module handles precise atom placement and coordinate transformations:

### Fourth Atom Placement

The `place_fourth_atom` function uses geometric constraints to determine atom positions:

```mermaid
graph TD
    INPUT_ATOMS["Three Known Atoms<br/>(A, B, C)"] --> CONSTRAINTS["Geometric Constraints"]
    CONSTRAINTS --> BOND_LENGTH["Bond Length"]
    CONSTRAINTS --> PLANAR_ANGLE["Planar Angle"] 
    CONSTRAINTS --> DIHEDRAL_ANGLE["Dihedral Angle"]
    
    BOND_LENGTH --> CALC["Coordinate Calculation"]
    PLANAR_ANGLE --> CALC
    DIHEDRAL_ANGLE --> CALC
    
    CALC --> BC_VEC["bc_vec = normalized(B-C)"]
    CALC --> N_VEC["n_vec = cross(B-A, bc_vec)"]
    CALC --> M_VEC["m_vec basis vectors"]
    
    BC_VEC --> D_COORD["Fourth Atom Position"]
    N_VEC --> D_COORD
    M_VEC --> D_COORD
```

**Sources:** [igfold/utils/coordinates.py:4-30]()

### Ideal Coordinates

Standard backbone geometry is provided through `get_ideal_coords` with ideal bond lengths and angles:

- N: `[0, 0, -1.458]`
- CA: `[0, 0, 0]` (reference point)
- CB: `[0, 1.426, 0.531]`
- C: Calculated using `place_fourth_atom`

**Sources:** [igfold/utils/coordinates.py:33-54]()

## Physical Constants

The `igfold.utils.constants` module defines standard structural parameters from Engh and Huber:

| Constant Type | Examples | Value (Å or degrees) |
|---------------|----------|---------------------|
| Bond Lengths | `BL_N_CA`, `BL_CA_C`, `BL_C_N` | 1.459, 1.525, 1.336 |
| Bond Angles | `BA_N_CA_C`, `BA_CA_C_N` | 111.0°, 117.2° |
| VdW Radii | `VDW_N`, `VDW_C` | 1.55, 1.7 |

**Sources:** [igfold/utils/constants.py:1-22]()

## AbNumber Integration

PDB renumbering uses the AbNumber web service for consistent antibody numbering:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant CLIENT as "renumber_pdb"
    participant ABNUM as "AbNum Web Service"
    participant FILE as "PDB File"
    
    CLIENT->>FILE: Read PDB file
    CLIENT->>ABNUM: POST pdb file with parameters
    Note over ABNUM: scheme="-c" (Chothia)<br/>output="-HL"<br/>plain="1"
    
    alt Success
        ABNUM-->>CLIENT: Renumbered PDB text
        CLIENT->>FILE: Write renumbered PDB
    else Failure
        ABNUM-->>CLIENT: Error response
        CLIENT->>CLIENT: Retry with exponential backoff
    end
```

**Sources:** [igfold/utils/pdb.py:21-59]()

## Structure Output

The `save_PDB` function writes coordinate tensors back to standard PDB format:

| Parameter | Purpose | Type |
|-----------|---------|------|
| `coords` | Atom coordinates | `torch.Tensor` |
| `seq` | Amino acid sequence | `str` |
| `chains` | Chain identifiers | `List[str]` |
| `error` | B-factor values | `torch.Tensor` |
| `delim` | Chain boundaries | `List[int]` |

The function handles chain assignment, residue numbering, and proper PDB formatting including TER and END records.

**Sources:** [igfold/utils/pdb.py:428-478]()

# Advanced Features

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

This page documents IgFold's advanced capabilities beyond basic structure prediction, including post-prediction refinement methods, specialized antibody analysis tools, and integration with external bioinformatics software. These features enable enhanced structure quality, domain-specific analysis, and customized workflows for specialized research applications.

For basic structure prediction workflows, see [Quick Start Guide](#3) and [User Guide](#4). For technical details on the core model architecture, see [Core Architecture](#5).

## Overview

IgFold provides several advanced features that extend beyond standard structure prediction:

- **Structure Refinement**: Post-prediction optimization using molecular dynamics and energy minimization
- **Antibody-Specific Tools**: Integration with specialized antibody analysis software
- **Advanced Analysis**: Enhanced metrics, validation, and visualization capabilities
- **External Tool Integration**: Seamless workflow integration with established bioinformatics tools

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Core Prediction"
        IGFOLD["IgFold.fold()"]
        COORDS["Raw Coordinates"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Structure Refinement"
        OPENMM_REF["openmm_ref.refine()"]

    end

        RENUMBERING["Chain Renumbering"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Advanced Output"
        REFINED_PDB["Refined PDB Structures"]
        PRMSD_ANALYSIS["pRMSD Analysis"]
        VISUALIZATION["3D Visualization"]
        VALIDATION["Structure Validation"]
    end
    
    IGFOLD --> COORDS
    COORDS --> OPENMM_REF
    COORDS --> PYROSETTA_REF
    
    OPENMM_REF --> MINIMIZATION
    PYROSETTA_REF --> MINIMIZATION
```

## Structure Refinement Pipeline

IgFold supports two primary refinement backends that can be applied after initial structure prediction to improve geometric quality and energy profiles.

### Refinement Workflow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    INPUT_PDB["Input PDB Structure"]
    
    subgraph "OpenMM Refinement"
        PDBFIXER["pdbfixer.PDBFixer"]
        MISSING_ATOMS["findMissingAtoms()"]
        ADD_HYDROGENS["addHydrogens()"]
        FORCE_FIELD["amber14/protein.ff14SB.xml"]
        CUSTOM_FORCE["CustomExternalForce"]
        HARMONIC_CONSTRAINTS["Harmonic Constraints"]
        ENERGY_MIN["minimizeEnergy()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "PyRosetta Refinement"
        POSE_IMPORT["pose_from_pdbstring()"]
        COORD_CST["AtomCoordinateCstMover"]
        MIN_MOVER["get_min_mover()"]
        SCORE_FUNCTION["ref2015_cst"]
        REPACK_MOVER["get_repack_mover()"]
        IDEALIZE_MOVER["IdealizeMover"]
    end
    
    INPUT_PDB --> PDBFIXER
    INPUT_PDB --> POSE_IMPORT
    
    PDBFIXER --> MISSING_ATOMS
    MISSING_ATOMS --> ADD_HYDROGENS
    ADD_HYDROGENS --> FORCE_FIELD
    FORCE_FIELD --> CUSTOM_FORCE
    CUSTOM_FORCE --> HARMONIC_CONSTRAINTS
    HARMONIC_CONSTRAINTS --> ENERGY_MIN
    
    POSE_IMPORT --> COORD_CST
    COORD_CST --> MIN_MOVER
    MIN_MOVER --> SCORE_FUNCTION
    SCORE_FUNCTION --> REPACK_MOVER
    REPACK_MOVER --> IDEALIZE_MOVER
    
    ENERGY_MIN --> OUTPUT_PDB["Refined PDB Structure"]
    IDEALIZE_MOVER --> OUTPUT_PDB
```

Sources: [igfold/refine/openmm_ref.py:7-44](), [igfold/refine/pyrosetta_ref.py:92-125]()

### Refinement Configuration Options

Both refinement backends provide configurable parameters for customizing the refinement process:

| Backend | Key Parameters | Description |
|---------|----------------|-------------|
| OpenMM | `stiffness` | Harmonic constraint strength (default: 10.0) |
| OpenMM | `tolerance` | Energy minimization tolerance (default: 2.39) |
| OpenMM | `use_gpu` | Enable GPU acceleration (default: False) |
| PyRosetta | `minimization_iter` | Maximum minimization iterations (default: 100) |
| PyRosetta | `constrain` | Apply coordinate constraints (default: True) |
| PyRosetta | `idealize` | Apply geometry idealization (default: False) |

### PyRosetta Refinement Components

The PyRosetta refinement system uses several specialized movers and scoring functions:

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Scoring Functions"
        REF2015["ref2015_cst"]
        CART_BONDED["cart_bonded weight"]
        COORD_CST["coordinate_constraint"]
        DIHED_CST["dihedral_constraint"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Movement Configuration"
        MOVEMAP["MoveMap"]
        BB_MOVES["set_bb(True)"]
        CHI_MOVES["set_chi(False)"]
        JUMP_MOVES["set_jump(False)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Refinement Movers"
        MIN_MOVER["MinMover"]
        RELAX_MOVER["FastRelax"]
        REPACK_MOVER["PackRotamersMover"]
        CST_MOVER["AtomCoordinateCstMover"]
    end
    
    REF2015 --> MIN_MOVER
    CART_BONDED --> MIN_MOVER
    COORD_CST --> MIN_MOVER
    DIHED_CST --> MIN_MOVER
    
    MOVEMAP --> MIN_MOVER
    BB_MOVES --> MOVEMAP
    CHI_MOVES --> MOVEMAP
    JUMP_MOVES --> MOVEMAP
    
    MIN_MOVER --> CST_MOVER
    RELAX_MOVER --> REPACK_MOVER
```

Sources: [igfold/refine/pyrosetta_ref.py:12-54](), [igfold/refine/pyrosetta_ref.py:57-89]()

## Advanced Configuration

Advanced users can customize IgFold's behavior through various configuration options and programmatic interfaces.

### Refinement Method Selection

The refinement backend can be selected and configured through the main API:

- **OpenMM Backend**: Molecular dynamics-based refinement with GPU acceleration support
- **PyRosetta Backend**: Rosetta-based refinement with advanced scoring functions
- **No Refinement**: Direct output of predicted coordinates

### Scoring and Constraint Configuration

PyRosetta refinement allows fine-tuning of scoring function weights:

| Score Term | Default Weight | Purpose |
|------------|----------------|---------|
| `cart_bonded` | 1.0 | Cartesian bonded geometry |
| `pro_close` | 0.0 | Proline closure (disabled) |
| `coordinate_constraint` | 1.0 | Position constraints |
| `dihedral_constraint` | 1.0 | Dihedral angle constraints |

### Minimization Parameters

Both backends support customizable minimization settings:

- **Iteration Limits**: Control computational cost vs. convergence
- **Constraint Strengths**: Balance refinement vs. structure preservation
- **Move Maps**: Specify which degrees of freedom to optimize

For detailed information on structure refinement methods, see [Structure Refinement](#6.1). For antibody-specific analysis tools and integrations, see [Antibody-Specific Tools](#6.2).

Sources: [igfold/refine/pyrosetta_ref.py:12-54](), [igfold/refine/openmm_ref.py:7-44]()

# Page: Structure Refinement

# Structure Refinement

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [igfold/__init__.py](igfold/__init__.py)
- [igfold/refine/openmm_ref.py](igfold/refine/openmm_ref.py)
- [igfold/refine/pyrosetta_ref.py](igfold/refine/pyrosetta_ref.py)

</details>



This document covers the post-prediction structure refinement capabilities in IgFold. Structure refinement is an optional post-processing step that applies physics-based energy minimization to improve the quality of predicted antibody structures. For information about the core structure prediction pipeline, see [5.2 Processing Pipeline](#5.2).

IgFold provides two refinement backends: OpenMM for lightweight constraint-based minimization and PyRosetta for comprehensive full-atom refinement with advanced molecular mechanics protocols.

## Overview

Structure refinement in IgFold addresses limitations inherent in neural network-based structure prediction by applying established computational biology methods to relax steric clashes, optimize side chain conformations, and improve overall geometric quality of predicted structures.

## Refinement Workflow

The refinement process operates as a post-processing step in the IgFold pipeline, taking predicted 3D coordinates and applying physics-based optimization:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    COORDS["Predicted Coordinates"] --> REFINE_CHOICE{"Refinement Method"}
    
    REFINE_CHOICE -->|"OpenMM"| OPENMM_FLOW["OpenMM Refinement"]
    REFINE_CHOICE -->|"PyRosetta"| PYROSETTA_FLOW["PyRosetta Refinement"]
    REFINE_CHOICE -->|"None"| OUTPUT["Final PDB Output"]
    
    OPENMM_FLOW --> PDBFIXER["PDBFixer.findMissingAtoms()"]
    PDBFIXER --> ADD_HYDROGENS["Modeller.addHydrogens()"]
    ADD_HYDROGENS --> FORCE_FIELD["ForceField.createSystem()"]
    FORCE_FIELD --> CONSTRAINTS["CustomExternalForce"]
    CONSTRAINTS --> MINIMIZE["simulation.minimizeEnergy()"]
    MINIMIZE --> OUTPUT
    
    PYROSETTA_FLOW --> INIT_POSE["pose_from_pdbstring()"]
    INIT_POSE --> COORD_CST["AtomCoordinateCstMover.apply()"]
    COORD_CST --> MIN_MOVER["MinMover.apply()"]
    MIN_MOVER --> IDEALIZE["IdealizeMover.apply()"]
    IDEALIZE --> REPACK["PackRotamersMover.apply()"]
    REPACK --> FINAL_MIN["MinMover.apply()"]
    FINAL_MIN --> OUTPUT
```

Sources: [igfold/refine/openmm_ref.py:1-44](), [igfold/refine/pyrosetta_ref.py:92-125]()

## OpenMM Refinement

OpenMM refinement provides lightweight structure optimization focused on resolving steric clashes while maintaining the overall predicted fold. The `refine` function in the OpenMM module implements constraint-based energy minimization.

### OpenMM Refinement Process

| Step | Function | Purpose |
|------|----------|---------|
| Structure Preparation | `pdbfixer.PDBFixer()` | Add missing atoms and residues |
| Hydrogen Addition | `modeller.addHydrogens()` | Add hydrogen atoms for complete structure |
| Force Field Setup | `ForceField.createSystem()` | Initialize AMBER14 force field |
| Constraint Application | `CustomExternalForce()` | Apply harmonic constraints to backbone atoms |
| Energy Minimization | `simulation.minimizeEnergy()` | Optimize structure geometry |

### OpenMM Configuration

The OpenMM refinement accepts several parameters:

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class OpenMMRefinement {
        +stiffness: float
        +tolerance: float
        +use_gpu: bool
        +refine(pdb_file, stiffness, tolerance, use_gpu)
    }
    
    class PDBFixer {
        +findMissingResidues()
        +findMissingAtoms()
        +addMissingAtoms()
    }
    
    class CustomExternalForce {
        +addGlobalParameter("k", stiffness)
        +addPerParticleParameter("x0")
        +addPerParticleParameter("y0") 
        +addPerParticleParameter("z0")
        +addParticle(atom_index, position)
    }
    
    OpenMMRefinement --> PDBFixer
    OpenMMRefinement --> CustomExternalForce
```

The harmonic constraints are applied to backbone atoms N, CA, C, and CB with force constant `k = stiffness * ENERGY / LENGTH²`. Default stiffness is 10 kcal/mol/Ų and tolerance is 2.39 kcal/mol.

Sources: [igfold/refine/openmm_ref.py:7-44]()

## PyRosetta Refinement

PyRosetta refinement provides comprehensive full-atom structure optimization using Rosetta's advanced molecular mechanics protocols. This backend offers more sophisticated refinement capabilities including side chain optimization and geometric idealization.

### PyRosetta Refinement Components

```mermaid
graph TD
    INIT["init_pyrosetta()"] --> POSE["pose_from_pdbstring()"]
    
    POSE --> CONSTRAIN{"constrain=True"}
    CONSTRAIN -->|"Yes"| CST_MOVER["AtomCoordinateCstMover"]
    CONSTRAIN -->|"No"| MIN_MOVER["get_min_mover()"]
    
    CST_MOVER --> MIN_MOVER
    MIN_MOVER --> MIN_APPLY["MinMover.apply()"]
    
    MIN_APPLY --> IDEALIZE_CHECK{"idealize=True"}
    IDEALIZE_CHECK -->|"Yes"| IDEALIZE_MOVER["IdealizeMover"]
    IDEALIZE_CHECK -->|"No"| REPACK_MOVER["get_repack_mover()"]
    
    IDEALIZE_MOVER --> REPACK_MOVER
    REPACK_MOVER --> REPACK_APPLY["PackRotamersMover.apply()"]
    REPACK_APPLY --> FINAL_MIN["MinMover.apply()"]
    FINAL_MIN --> DUMP["pose.dump_pdb()"]
```

### PyRosetta Movers and Score Functions

| Component | Class | Configuration | Purpose |
|-----------|-------|---------------|---------|
| Minimizer | `MinMover` | L-BFGS-Armijo, Cartesian | Backbone optimization |
| Score Function | `ref2015_cst` | Coordinate/dihedral constraints | Energy evaluation |
| Relaxer | `FastRelax` | Full-atom relax protocol | Comprehensive optimization |
| Packer | `PackRotamersMover` | Restrict to repacking | Side chain optimization |

The `get_min_mover` function creates a minimization mover with customizable constraint weights:

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class MinMover {
        +max_iter: int
        +sf_name: str  
        +coord_cst_weight: float
        +dih_cst_weight: float
        +set_weight(ScoreType, weight)
        +cartesian(True)
        +max_iter(1000)
    }
    
    class MoveMap {
        +set_bb(True)
        +set_chi(False) 
        +set_jump(False)
    }
    
    class ScoreFunction {
        +cart_bonded: 1.0
        +pro_close: 0.0
        +coordinate_constraint: coord_cst_weight
        +dihedral_constraint: dih_cst_weight
    }
    
    MinMover --> MoveMap
    MinMover --> ScoreFunction
```

Sources: [igfold/refine/pyrosetta_ref.py:12-54](), [igfold/refine/pyrosetta_ref.py:92-125]()

## Refinement Integration

Structure refinement integrates with the main IgFold prediction pipeline as an optional post-processing step. The refinement choice is typically specified through the `IgFoldRunner` interface, which coordinates the refinement process after structure prediction is complete.

### Refinement Pipeline Integration

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Runner as "IgFoldRunner"
    participant Model as "IgFold Model"
    participant OpenMM as "openmm_ref.refine()"
    participant PyRosetta as "pyrosetta_ref.refine()"
    participant Output as "PDB Output"
    
    Runner->>Model: "fold(sequences, template)"
    Model-->>Runner: "coordinates + pRMSD"
    
    alt "OpenMM Refinement"
        Runner->>OpenMM: "refine(pdb_file, stiffness, tolerance)"
        OpenMM-->>Runner: "refined structure"
    else "PyRosetta Refinement"  
        Runner->>PyRosetta: "refine(pdb_string, constrain, idealize)"
        PyRosetta-->>Runner: "refined structure"
    else "No Refinement"
        Runner->>Output: "raw predicted structure"
    end
    
    Runner->>Output: "final PDB structure"
```

### Refinement Method Selection

The refinement backend selection depends on the intended use case and available computational resources:

| Method | Computational Cost | Use Case | Key Features |
|--------|-------------------|----------|--------------|
| None | Minimal | Fast prediction, analysis | Raw neural network output |
| OpenMM | Low-Medium | Production use, moderate quality | Constraint-based minimization |
| PyRosetta | High | High-quality structures, detailed analysis | Full-atom optimization, side chain packing |

Both refinement methods preserve the overall fold predicted by the IgFold neural network while improving local geometry and reducing energy.

Sources: [igfold/refine/openmm_ref.py:1-44](), [igfold/refine/pyrosetta_ref.py:1-125]()

# Page: Antibody-Specific Tools

# Antibody-Specific Tools

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [igfold/utils/ab_metrics.py](igfold/utils/ab_metrics.py)
- [igfold/utils/abnumber_.py](igfold/utils/abnumber_.py)

</details>



This section covers IgFold's integration with specialized antibody analysis tools, primarily the AbNumber library for antibody numbering and CDR identification, as well as PyRosetta-based metrics for structural analysis. These tools provide antibody-specific functionality beyond the core structure prediction capabilities.

For core structure prediction capabilities, see [IgFoldRunner API](#4.1). For general structure refinement options, see [Structure Refinement](#6.1).

## AbNumber Integration Architecture

IgFold integrates with the AbNumber library to provide standardized antibody numbering schemes, chain type identification, and CDR region analysis. The integration is primarily handled through utility functions that process both sequences and structures.

**AbNumber Processing Pipeline**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    INPUT_SEQ["Antibody Sequence"] --> IS_HEAVY["is_heavy()"]
    INPUT_PDB["PDB Structure"] --> RECHAIN["rechain_pdb()"]
    
    IS_HEAVY --> CHAIN_OBJ["abnumber.Chain()"]
    RECHAIN --> PARSER["Bio.PDB.PDBParser"]
    
    CHAIN_OBJ --> CHAIN_TYPE["Heavy/Light Classification"]
    PARSER --> EXTRACT_SEQ["Extract Sequence from PDB"]
    
    EXTRACT_SEQ --> ABNUMBER_CHAIN["abnumber.Chain()"]
    ABNUMBER_CHAIN --> POSITIONS["positions.items()"]
    
    POSITIONS --> RENUMBER_PDB["renumber_pdb()"]
    POSITIONS --> TRUNCATE_SEQ["truncate_seq()"]
    
    RENUMBER_PDB --> NUMBERED_PDB["Renumbered PDB File"]
    TRUNCATE_SEQ --> CLEAN_SEQ["Cleaned Sequence"]
    
    NUMBERED_PDB --> PDBIO["Bio.PDB.PDBIO"]
    PDBIO --> OUTPUT_PDB["Output PDB"]
```

Sources: [igfold/utils/abnumber_.py:9-88]()

## Chain Type Identification

The `is_heavy()` function determines whether an antibody sequence corresponds to a heavy or light chain using AbNumber's classification system.

**Chain Identification Process**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    SEQ["Input Sequence"] --> CHAIN_CREATE["Chain(seq, scheme='chothia')"]
    CHAIN_CREATE --> IS_HEAVY_CHECK["is_heavy_chain()"]
    IS_HEAVY_CHECK --> HEAVY_RESULT["True/False"]
    
    HEAVY_RESULT --> H_CHAIN["Heavy Chain"]
    HEAVY_RESULT --> L_CHAIN["Light Chain"]
```

The function uses the Chothia numbering scheme by default and leverages AbNumber's built-in heavy chain detection algorithms.

| Function | Purpose | Returns |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `is_heavy(seq)` | Classify chain type | Boolean (True=Heavy, False=Light) |
| `Chain(seq, scheme='chothia')` | Create AbNumber chain object | AbNumber Chain instance |
| `is_heavy_chain()` | AbNumber classification method | Boolean classification |

Sources: [igfold/utils/abnumber_.py:9-12]()

## PDB Structure Renumbering

The renumbering system provides two main capabilities: chain ID assignment and residue renumbering according to standard antibody numbering schemes.

**PDB Renumbering Workflow**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    INPUT_PDB["Input PDB File"] --> CLEAN_PDB["clean_pdb()"]
    CLEAN_PDB --> PARSE_STRUCT["PDBParser.get_structure()"]
    
    PARSE_STRUCT --> ITER_CHAINS["Iterate Chains"]
    ITER_CHAINS --> EXTRACT_SEQ_CHAIN["Extract Chain Sequence"]
    
    EXTRACT_SEQ_CHAIN --> CREATE_ABNUMBER["Chain(seq, scheme)"]
    CREATE_ABNUMBER --> GET_POSITIONS["positions.items()"]
    
    GET_POSITIONS --> VALIDATE_LENGTH["Assert len(chain_res) == len(numbering)"]
    VALIDATE_LENGTH --> ITER_RESIDUES["Iterate Residues"]
    
    ITER_RESIDUES --> VALIDATE_AA["Validate Amino Acid Match"]
    VALIDATE_AA --> PARSE_POSITION["Parse Position & Insertion"]
    
    PARSE_POSITION --> UPDATE_ID["Update residue._id"]
    UPDATE_ID --> NEXT_RESIDUE["Next Residue"]
    NEXT_RESIDUE --> ITER_RESIDUES
    
    ITER_RESIDUES --> SAVE_STRUCT["PDBIO.save()"]
    SAVE_STRUCT --> OUTPUT_PDB["Renumbered PDB"]
```

**Chain Re-identification Process**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    PDB_CHAINS["PDB Chain Objects"] --> EXTRACT_SEQ["seq1(residue.resname)"]
    EXTRACT_SEQ --> ABNUMBER_OBJ["abnumber.Chain()"]
    
    ABNUMBER_OBJ --> CHAIN_TYPE["is_heavy_chain()"]
    CHAIN_TYPE --> SET_ID_H["Set chain.id = 'H'"]
    CHAIN_TYPE --> SET_ID_L["Set chain.id = 'L'"]
    
    SET_ID_H --> HANDLE_CONFLICT["Handle ValueError"]
    SET_ID_L --> HANDLE_CONFLICT
    
    HANDLE_CONFLICT --> TEMP_ID["chain.id = 'H_' or 'L_'"]
    TEMP_ID --> CLEANUP["Remove '_' suffix"]
    CLEANUP --> FINAL_CHAINS["Final Chain IDs"]
```

| Function | Parameters | Purpose |
|----------|------------|---------|
| `rechain_pdb(pdb_file)` | PDB file path | Assigns H/L chain IDs |
| `renumber_pdb(in_pdb_file, out_pdb_file, scheme)` | Input PDB, output PDB, numbering scheme | Renumbers residues |
| `truncate_seq(seq, scheme)` | Sequence, numbering scheme | Truncates sequence to numbered positions |

Sources: [igfold/utils/abnumber_.py:15-88]()

## Sequence Processing Functions

The sequence processing utilities handle antibody-specific sequence manipulations that align with standard numbering conventions.

### Truncation Function

The `truncate_seq()` function processes sequences to include only positions that have valid AbNumber assignments:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    INPUT_SEQ["Input Sequence"] --> CREATE_CHAIN["Chain(seq, scheme)"]
    CREATE_CHAIN --> GET_POSITIONS["positions.items()"]
    GET_POSITIONS --> EXTRACT_AA["Extract Amino Acids"]
    EXTRACT_AA --> JOIN_SEQ["''.join([r[1] for r in numbering])"]
    JOIN_SEQ --> CLEAN_SEQ["Truncated Sequence"]
```

This ensures that processed sequences contain only residues with valid numbering positions, removing any terminal extensions or non-standard regions.

Sources: [igfold/utils/abnumber_.py:83-88]()

## PyRosetta-based Antibody Analysis

The `ab_metrics.py` module provides advanced structural analysis capabilities using PyRosetta's antibody-specific tools.

**PyRosetta Antibody Analysis Pipeline**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    POSE_INPUT["PyRosetta Pose"] --> ANTIBODY_INFO["AntibodyInfo(pose)"]
    
    ANTIBODY_INFO --> VH_VL_ORIENT["vl_vh_orientation_coords()"]
    ANTIBODY_INFO --> CDR_RMSD["cdr_backbone_rmsds()"]
    ANTIBODY_INFO --> CDR_CLUSTERS["setup_CDR_clusters()"]
    
    VH_VL_ORIENT --> ORIENT_METRICS["VL-VH Distance, Opening Angle, etc."]
    CDR_RMSD --> RMSD_METRICS["H1/H2/H3 and L1/L2/L3 RMSDs"]
    CDR_CLUSTERS --> CLUSTER_ASSIGN["CDR Cluster Assignments"]
    
    ORIENT_METRICS --> RESULTS_DICT["Results Dictionary"]
    RMSD_METRICS --> RESULTS_DICT
    CLUSTER_ASSIGN --> RESULTS_DICT
```

### Structural Metrics

| Function | Returns | Metrics |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `get_vh_vl_orientation(pose)` | Dictionary | VL-VH distance, opening angle, opposite angle, packing angle |
| `get_ab_metrics(pose1, pose2)` | Dictionary | OCD, FRH/FRL RMSD, H1/H2/H3 RMSD, L1/L2/L3 RMSD |
| `get_pose_cdr_clusters(pose)` | Dictionary | CDR cluster assignments (H1-H3, L1-L3) |

### CDR Analysis Details

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    CDR_ENUM["CDRNameEnum(1-6)"] --> GET_CLUSTER["get_CDR_cluster()"]
    GET_CLUSTER --> CLUSTER_RESULT["cluster.cluster()"]
    CLUSTER_RESULT --> CLUSTER_NAME["get_cluster_name()"]
    CLUSTER_NAME --> FINAL_CLUSTER["CDR Cluster Assignment"]
    
    MAPPING["clus_name = {1: 'h1', 2: 'h2', 3: 'h3', 4: 'l1', 5: 'l2', 6: 'l3'}"]
```

Sources: [igfold/utils/ab_metrics.py:1-60]()

## Integration with IgFold Pipeline

These antibody-specific tools integrate with IgFold's main prediction pipeline through optional post-processing steps and validation utilities.

**Pipeline Integration Points**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    IGFOLD_PRED["IgFold Prediction"] --> PDB_OUTPUT["PDB Structure"]
    
    PDB_OUTPUT --> OPT_RECHAIN["Optional: rechain_pdb()"]
    PDB_OUTPUT --> OPT_RENUMBER["Optional: renumber_pdb()"]
    
    OPT_RECHAIN --> VALIDATION["Chain ID Validation"]
    OPT_RENUMBER --> STANDARD_NUM["Standard Numbering"]
    
    VALIDATION --> DOWNSTREAM["Downstream Analysis"]
    STANDARD_NUM --> DOWNSTREAM
    
    DOWNSTREAM --> PYROSETTA_ANALYSIS["Optional: PyRosetta Metrics"]
    PYROSETTA_ANALYSIS --> FINAL_RESULTS["Final Analysis Results"]
```

The integration typically occurs during the refinement phase, where structures can be automatically renumbered and validated before final output.

### Configuration Options

When using these tools with IgFold, several parameters control the antibody-specific processing:

| Parameter | Options | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|---------|
| `scheme` | 'chothia', 'kabat', 'imgt' | Numbering scheme for renumbering |
| `rechain` | Boolean | Whether to reassign chain IDs |
| `renumber` | Boolean | Whether to renumber residues |

Sources: [igfold/utils/abnumber_.py:37-88](), [igfold/utils/ab_metrics.py:1-60]()

## Training and Loss Function Systems

The training system implements geometric loss functions that enforce protein structural constraints while enabling gradient-based optimization of 3D coordinates.

### Geometric Loss Functions

The training utilities provide several specialized loss functions for structural validation:

| Function | Purpose | Key Parameters |
|----------|---------|----------------|
| `kabsch_mse()` | Optimal alignment RMSE | `align_mask`, `clamp`, `sqrt` |
| `bond_len_loss()` | Bond length constraints | `seq_lens`, `mask` |
| `bond_angle_loss()` | Bond angle constraints | `seq_lens`, `mask` |
| `vdw_clash_loss()` | Van der Waals clash detection | `tol=1.5` |
| `violation_loss()` | Combined structural violations | `seq_lens`, `mask` |

The `violation_loss()` function [igfold/training/utils.py:277-286]() combines all structural constraints:

```python
def violation_loss(pred, seq_lens, mask, eps=EPS):
    bl_loss = bond_len_loss(pred, seq_lens, mask, eps=eps)
    ba_loss = bond_angle_loss(pred, seq_lens, mask, eps=eps)
    vdw_loss = vdw_clash_loss(pred, mask)
    cis_loss = cis_peptide_loss(pred, seq_lens, mask, eps=eps)
    loss = bl_loss + ba_loss + vdw_loss + cis_loss
    return loss
```

**Sources:** [igfold/training/utils.py:194-286]()

### Kabsch Alignment System

The Kabsch algorithm implementation [igfold/training/utils.py:11-76]() provides optimal superposition for structure comparison:

```mermaid
graph LR
    MOBILE["mobile coords"] --> KABSCH["kabsch()"]
    STATIONARY["stationary coords"] --> KABSCH
    KABSCH --> TRANSFORM["transformation"]
    KABSCH --> ALIGNED["aligned coords"]
    
    ALIGNED --> DO_KABSCH["do_kabsch()"]
    ALIGN_MASK["align_mask"] --> DO_KABSCH
    
    DO_KABSCH --> KABSCH_MSE["kabsch_mse()"]
    MASK["mask"] --> KABSCH_MSE
    KABSCH_MSE --> LOSS["RMSE loss"]
```

**Sources:** [igfold/training/utils.py:11-136]()

- `kabsch_mse()` for alignment quality [igfold/training/utils.py:100-136]()
- `violation_loss()` for structural constraints [igfold/training/utils.py:277-286]()

## Component Architecture Overview

The IgFold model is built from several key neural network components that work together to process antibody sequences and predict 3D structures:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Attention Mechanisms"
```

## Invariant Point Attention (IPA)

The core innovation of IgFold is the Invariant Point Attention mechanism, which processes both sequence representations and 3D geometric information while maintaining rotational and translational invariance.

### InvariantPointAttention Class

The `InvariantPointAttention` class implements a specialized attention mechanism that operates in both sequence space and 3D coordinate space:

| Parameter | Purpose | Default |
|-----------|---------|---------|
| `dim` | Input feature dimension | Required |
| `heads` | Number of attention heads | 8 |
| `scalar_key_dim` | Dimension for scalar attention keys | 16 |
| `scalar_value_dim` | Dimension for scalar attention values | 16 |
| `point_key_dim` | Dimension for point attention keys | 4 |
| `point_value_dim` | Dimension for point attention values | 4 |
| `pairwise_repr_dim` | Pairwise representation dimension | `dim` |

The attention computation combines three types of logits:
- **Scalar attention**: Standard dot-product attention on sequence features
- **Point attention**: Distance-based attention in 3D coordinate space  
- **Pairwise attention**: Bias from pairwise sequence representations

Sources: [igfold/model/components/IPABlock.py:34-196]()

### IPABlock Architecture

The `IPABlock` combines `InvariantPointAttention` with feedforward layers and normalization:

```mermaid
graph LR
    Input["Input Features<br/>(b, n, dim)"] --> AN["LayerNorm<br/>(attn_norm)"]
    AN --> IPA["InvariantPointAttention"]
    Input --> Add1["+"]
    IPA --> Add1
    Add1 --> FN["LayerNorm<br/>(ff_norm)"]
    FN --> FF["FeedForward<br/>(3 layers)"]
    Add1 --> Add2["+"]
    FF --> Add2
    Add2 --> Output["Output Features<br/>(b, n, dim)"]
```

Sources: [igfold/model/components/IPABlock.py:219-248]()

## Transformer Architectures

### IPATransformer

The `IPATransformer` is the primary structure-generating component that iteratively refines 3D coordinates through multiple IPA layers:

```mermaid
graph TB
    SR["single_repr<br/>(b, n, dim)"] --> Layer1["IPABlock + Linear"]
    T0["translations<br/>(b, n, 3)"] --> Layer1
    Q0["quaternions<br/>(b, n, 4)"] --> QTM1["quaternion_to_matrix"]
    QTM1 --> R1["rotations<br/>(b, n, 3, 3)"]
    R1 --> Layer1
    
    Layer1 --> Updates1["quaternion_update<br/>translation_update"]
    Updates1 --> QM1["quaternion_multiply"]
    Updates1 --> T1["Updated translations"]
    Q0 --> QM1
    QM1 --> Q1["Updated quaternions"]
    
    Q1 --> Layer2["IPABlock + Linear"]
    T1 --> Layer2
    Layer2 --> Updates2["..."]
    
    Updates2 --> FinalCoords["get_ideal_coords +<br/>place_o_coords"]
    FinalCoords --> Points["points_global<br/>(b, n, atoms, 3)"]
```

The key operations include:
- Converting quaternions to rotation matrices via `quaternion_to_matrix`
- Updating poses through `quaternion_multiply` and translation updates
- Generating final atomic coordinates with `get_ideal_coords` and `place_o_coords`

Sources: [igfold/model/components/IPATransformer.py:55-175]()

### GraphTransformer

The `GraphTransformer` processes node and edge representations using standard attention mechanisms:

| Component | Class | Purpose |
|-----------|-------|---------|
| `Attention` | Graph attention layer | Processes nodes with edge bias |
| `FeedForward` | MLP with GELU activation | Node feature transformation |
| `GatedResidual` | Gated residual connection | Adaptive residual weighting |
| `PreNorm` | Layer normalization | Input normalization |

The attention mechanism incorporates edge information by adding edge features to keys and values:

```python
# From GraphTransformer.py lines 140-141
k = k + ek  # Add edge features to keys
v = v + ev  # Add edge features to values
```

Sources: [igfold/model/components/GraphTransformer.py:70-255]()

## Specialized Modules

### TriangleMultiplicativeModule

This module implements the triangle multiplicative update from AlphaFold, which updates pairwise representations through multiplicative interactions:

```mermaid
graph LR
    X["Input<br/>(b, n, n, dim)"] --> Norm["LayerNorm"]
    Norm --> LP["left_proj"]
    Norm --> RP["right_proj"]
    Norm --> LG["left_gate"]
    Norm --> RG["right_gate"]
    Norm --> OG["out_gate"]
    
    LP --> LGate["sigmoid"]
    RP --> RGate["sigmoid"]
    LG --> LGate
    RG --> RGate
    OG --> OutGate["sigmoid"]
    
    LGate --> Einsum["einsum<br/>(mix equation)"]
    RGate --> Einsum
    Einsum --> OutNorm["LayerNorm"]
    OutNorm --> ToOut["Linear"]
    ToOut --> OutGate
    OutGate --> Output["Output<br/>(b, n, n, dim)"]
```

The module supports two mixing patterns:
- **Outgoing**: `'... i k d, ... j k d -> ... i j d'`
- **Ingoing**: `'... k j d, ... k i d -> ... i j d'`

Sources: [igfold/model/components/TriangleMultiplicativeModule.py:12-109]()

### TriangleGraphTransformer

Combines graph attention with triangle multiplicative updates in alternating layers:

```mermaid
graph TB
    Input["nodes, edges"] --> GT["GraphTransformer"]
    GT --> Nodes1["Updated nodes"]
    GT --> Edges1["edges"]
    Edges1 --> TriOut["TriangleMultiplicativeModule<br/>(outgoing)"]
    TriOut --> Edges2["edges + tri_out"]
    Edges2 --> TriIn["TriangleMultiplicativeModule<br/>(ingoing)"]
    TriIn --> Edges3["edges + tri_in"]
    
    Nodes1 --> NextLayer["Next Layer"]
    Edges3 --> NextLayer
```

Sources: [igfold/model/components/TriangleGraphTransformer.py:8-62]()

## Geometric Transformations

The model relies heavily on quaternion-based rotations and geometric transformations for maintaining 3D structure consistency:

### Core Transform Functions

| Function | Input | Output | Purpose |
|----------|-------|--------|---------|
| `quaternion_to_matrix` | `(*, 4)` | `(*, 3, 3)` | Convert quaternions to rotation matrices |
| `quaternion_multiply` | `(*, 4)`, `(*, 4)` | `(*, 4)` | Compose rotations |
| `matrix_to_quaternion` | `(*, 3, 3)` | `(*, 4)` | Convert rotation matrices to quaternions |
| `rotation_6d_to_matrix` | `(*, 6)` | `(*, 3, 3)` | Convert 6D rotation representation |
| `quaternion_apply` | `(*, 4)`, `(*, 3)` | `(*, 3)` | Apply rotation to 3D points |

### Quaternion Operations

The quaternion operations maintain numerical stability and standard form:

```python
# From transforms.py lines 331-345
def quaternion_multiply(a: torch.Tensor, b: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Multiply quaternions representing rotations with standardization"""
    ab = quaternion_raw_multiply(a, b)
    return standardize_quaternion(ab)  # Ensure non-negative real part
```

Sources: [igfold/utils/transforms.py:37-521]()

## Component Integration Patterns

The model components follow several key integration patterns:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Structure Generation Pipeline"
        SeqRepr["Sequence Representations"] --> GT["GraphTransformer"]
        GT --> NodeFeats["Node Features"]
        NodeFeats --> IPATrans["IPATransformer"]
        IPATrans --> Coords["3D Coordinates"]
        
        PairRepr["Pairwise Representations"] --> GT
        PairRepr --> IPA["InvariantPointAttention"]
        IPA --> IPATrans
        
        Templates["Template Coordinates"] --> IPATrans
    end
    
    subgraph "Geometric Consistency"
        Coords --> QT["quaternion_to_matrix"]
        QT --> Rotations["Rotation Matrices"]
        Rotations --> IPA
        IPATrans --> QM["quaternion_multiply"]
        QM --> IPATrans
    end
    
    subgraph "Feature Processing"
        NodeFeats --> FF1["FeedForward"]
        FF1 --> NodeFeats
        PairRepr --> TMM["TriangleMultiplicativeModule"]
        TMM --> PairRepr
    end
```

Key design principles:
- **Geometric consistency**: All operations preserve rotational/translational invariance
- **Iterative refinement**: Multiple layers progressively improve structure predictions  
- **Multi-scale processing**: Combines local (attention) and global (geometric) information
- **Residual connections**: Enable stable deep architectures with gradient flow

Sources: [igfold/model/components/IPATransformer.py:55-175](), [igfold/model/components/GraphTransformer.py:187-255](), [igfold/model/components/TriangleGraphTransformer.py:45-62]()

# Page: Training and Loss Functions

# Training and Loss Functions

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [igfold/model/components/IPABlock.py](igfold/model/components/IPABlock.py)
- [igfold/model/components/IPATransformer.py](igfold/model/components/IPATransformer.py)
- [igfold/training/utils.py](igfold/training/utils.py)
- [igfold/utils/constants.py](igfold/utils/constants.py)
- [igfold/utils/geometry.py](igfold/utils/geometry.py)
- [igfold/utils/transforms.py](igfold/utils/transforms.py)

</details>



This document covers the training utilities, loss functions, and structural validation metrics used in IgFold's deep learning pipeline. These components are responsible for optimizing the neural network models during training and evaluating the quality of predicted protein structures against ground truth data.

For information about the core model architecture that these loss functions train, see [Model Components](#7.1). For the overall processing pipeline, see [Processing Pipeline](#5.2).

## Overview of Training Components

IgFold's training system incorporates specialized loss functions designed for protein structure prediction, focusing on geometric constraints, structural validity, and alignment-based metrics. The training utilities handle the complex requirements of 3D protein structure optimization.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Training Pipeline"
        PRED["Predicted Coordinates"]
        TARGET["Target Coordinates"]
        MASK["Sequence Masks"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Alignment Utilities"
        KABSCH["kabsch()"]
        DO_KABSCH["do_kabsch()"]
        KABSCH_MSE["kabsch_mse()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Structural Loss Functions"
        BOND_LEN["bond_len_loss()"]
        BOND_ANG["bond_angle_loss()"]
        VDW_CLASH["vdw_clash_loss()"]
        CIS_PEP["cis_peptide_loss()"]
        VIOLATION["violation_loss()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Quality Metrics"
        BB_PRMSD["bb_prmsd_l1()"]
        BOND_L1["bond_length_l1()"]
    end
    
    PRED --> KABSCH_MSE
    TARGET --> KABSCH_MSE
    KABSCH_MSE --> KABSCH
    KABSCH_MSE --> DO_KABSCH
    
    PRED --> BOND_LEN
    PRED --> BOND_ANG
    PRED --> VDW_CLASH
    PRED --> CIS_PEP
    
    BOND_LEN --> VIOLATION
    BOND_ANG --> VIOLATION
    VDW_CLASH --> VIOLATION
    CIS_PEP --> VIOLATION
    
    PRED --> BB_PRMSD
    TARGET --> BB_PRMSD
    PRED --> BOND_L1
    TARGET --> BOND_L1
    
    MASK --> BOND_LEN
    MASK --> BOND_ANG
    MASK --> VDW_CLASH
    MASK --> CIS_PEP
```

Sources: [igfold/training/utils.py:1-287]()

## Core Loss Functions

### Kabsch-Based Alignment Loss

The primary loss function for structure prediction uses Kabsch alignment to optimally superpose predicted and target structures before computing the mean squared error.

| Function | Purpose | Key Parameters |
|----------|---------|----------------|
| `kabsch()` | Optimal rigid-body alignment | `mobile`, `stationary`, `return_translation_rotation` |
| `do_kabsch()` | Apply Kabsch transformation | `mobile`, `stationary`, `align_mask` |
| `kabsch_mse()` | MSE loss after alignment | `pred`, `target`, `align_mask`, `clamp`, `sqrt` |

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    MOBILE["Mobile Coordinates"]
    STATIONARY["Stationary Coordinates"]
    ALIGN_MASK["Alignment Mask"]
    
    MOBILE --> KABSCH["kabsch()"]
    STATIONARY --> KABSCH
    
    KABSCH --> SVD["SVD Decomposition"]
    SVD --> ROTATION["Rotation Matrix U"]
    SVD --> TRANSLATION["Translation Vectors"]
    
    ROTATION --> TRANSFORM["Transform Function"]
    TRANSLATION --> TRANSFORM
    
    MOBILE --> DO_KABSCH["do_kabsch()"]
    STATIONARY --> DO_KABSCH
    ALIGN_MASK --> DO_KABSCH
    
    DO_KABSCH --> KABSCH
    DO_KABSCH --> ALIGNED["Aligned Coordinates"]
    
    ALIGNED --> MSE["kabsch_mse()"]
    STATIONARY --> MSE
    MSE --> LOSS["Final Loss"]
```

The `kabsch()` function implements the Kabsch algorithm using SVD decomposition to find the optimal rotation and translation matrices. For PyTorch versions prior to 1.8, it handles the transpose requirement for the W matrix from `torch.svd()`.

Sources: [igfold/training/utils.py:11-76](), [igfold/training/utils.py:78-98](), [igfold/training/utils.py:100-137]()

### Structural Validation Losses

IgFold incorporates multiple structural validation loss functions that enforce protein geometry constraints:

#### Bond Length Loss
```python
bond_len_loss(pred, seq_lens, mask, eps=EPS)
```
Enforces ideal bond lengths for backbone atoms (N-CA, CA-C, C-N bonds) using literature values from Engh and Huber constants.

#### Bond Angle Loss  
```python
bond_angle_loss(pred, seq_lens, mask, eps=EPS)
```
Validates backbone bond angles, specifically CA-C-N and C-N-CA angles, using cosine-based loss functions.

#### Van der Waals Clash Loss
```python
vdw_clash_loss(pred, mask, tol=1.5, eps=EPS)  
```
Prevents atomic clashes by penalizing violations of van der Waals radii with a specified tolerance.

#### Cis-Peptide Loss
```python
cis_peptide_loss(pred, seq_lens, mask, eps=EPS)
```
Enforces trans-peptide bond geometry by penalizing deviations from the expected π dihedral angle.

Sources: [igfold/training/utils.py:194-219](), [igfold/training/utils.py:221-241](), [igfold/training/utils.py:243-261](), [igfold/training/utils.py:263-275]()

### Combined Violation Loss

The `violation_loss()` function combines all structural validation losses into a single comprehensive metric:

```mermaid
graph TD
    PRED["Predicted Structure"]
    SEQ_LENS["Sequence Lengths"]
    MASK["Structure Mask"]
    
    PRED --> BL["bond_len_loss()"]
    PRED --> BA["bond_angle_loss()"]
    PRED --> VDW["vdw_clash_loss()"]
    PRED --> CIS["cis_peptide_loss()"]
    
    SEQ_LENS --> BL
    SEQ_LENS --> BA
    SEQ_LENS --> CIS
    
    MASK --> BL
    MASK --> BA
    MASK --> VDW
    MASK --> CIS
    
    BL --> TOTAL["Total Violation Loss"]
    BA --> TOTAL
    VDW --> TOTAL
    CIS --> TOTAL
```

Sources: [igfold/training/utils.py:277-287]()

## Quality Metrics and Evaluation

### Predicted RMSD Loss

The `bb_prmsd_l1()` function evaluates the accuracy of predicted per-residue RMSD values against actual structural deviations:

```python
bb_prmsd_l1(pdev, pred, target, align_mask=None, mask=None)
```

This function compares predicted deviation values (`pdev`) with actual backbone deviations computed after Kabsch alignment, using L1 loss for robustness.

### Bond Length Validation

The `bond_length_l1()` function provides detailed bond length validation with configurable offset analysis:

```python
bond_length_l1(pred, target, mask, offsets=[1, 2])
```

This evaluates bond lengths at different sequence separations (1-bond, 2-bond distances) using L1 loss.

Sources: [igfold/training/utils.py:159-193](), [igfold/training/utils.py:139-157]()

## Geometric Utilities Integration

The training system leverages geometric calculation utilities for loss computation:

| Utility Function | Purpose | Source Module |
|------------------|---------|---------------|
| `dist()` | Euclidean distance | `igfold.utils.geometry` |
| `angle()` | Bond angle calculation | `igfold.utils.geometry` |  
| `dihedral()` | Dihedral angle calculation | `igfold.utils.geometry` |
| Constants (BL_*, BA_*, VDW_*) | Literature geometry values | `igfold.utils.constants` |

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Constants"
        BL_N_CA["BL_N_CA = 1.459"]
        BL_CA_C["BL_CA_C = 1.525"] 
        BL_C_N["BL_C_N = 1.336"]
        BA_CA_C_N["BA_CA_C_N = 117.2"]
        BA_C_N_CA["BA_C_N_CA = 121.7"]
        VDW_N["VDW_N = 1.55"]
        VDW_C["VDW_C = 1.7"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Geometry Functions"
        DIST["dist()"]
        ANGLE["angle()"]
        DIHEDRAL["dihedral()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Loss Functions"
        BOND_LEN_LOSS["bond_len_loss()"]
        BOND_ANG_LOSS["bond_angle_loss()"]
        VDW_LOSS["vdw_clash_loss()"]
        CIS_LOSS["cis_peptide_loss()"]
    end
    
    BL_N_CA --> BOND_LEN_LOSS
    BL_CA_C --> BOND_LEN_LOSS
    BL_C_N --> BOND_LEN_LOSS
    BA_CA_C_N --> BOND_ANG_LOSS
    BA_C_N_CA --> BOND_ANG_LOSS
    VDW_N --> VDW_LOSS
    VDW_C --> VDW_LOSS
    
    DIST --> BOND_LEN_LOSS
    ANGLE --> BOND_ANG_LOSS
    DIHEDRAL --> CIS_LOSS
```

Sources: [igfold/utils/geometry.py:23-28](), [igfold/utils/geometry.py:38-44](), [igfold/utils/geometry.py:46-58](), [igfold/utils/constants.py:1-22]()

## Model Integration

These loss functions operate on the output of IgFold's neural network components, particularly the coordinate predictions from the `IPATransformer` and related modules:

- **IPATransformer**: Produces final 3D coordinates (`points_global`) that serve as input to loss functions
- **IPABlock**: Provides intermediate representations used in deviation prediction
- **Structural Outputs**: Include translations, quaternions, and per-atom coordinates that are validated against geometric constraints

The training system expects predictions in the format `(batch, length, atoms, dimensions)` where atoms typically represent the backbone atoms N, CA, C, CB for each residue.

Sources: [igfold/model/components/IPATransformer.py:154-174](), [igfold/training/utils.py:194-287]()
